text: Agile methodology is a modern way of managing projects, especially in software development. Instead of planning everything at once, teams work in short cycles called sprints, which usually last two to four weeks. Before each sprint, the team chooses tasks from a prioritized list known as the backlog. These tasks are often written as user stories, which describe what a user needs from the product. During the sprint, team members hold daily standups—short meetings to share progress and problems. This iterative development approach helps teams adapt to changes quickly, improve communication, and deliver useful results to customers more often.
